comments.name: Jake
comments.body:
Lots of changes with JR East since the new CEO came in in 2024. 

Odd this article doesn't delve into the set up for the penguin, which was created by an Japanese artist, Chiharu Sakazaki, and licensed by Dentsu, a massive Japanese advertising agency which has built up the penguin's image over the years. 

Dentsu built up the image and has joint licensing with JR East. Much talk about the JR East CEO being eager to end licensing expenses to Dentsu and the artist and develop their own in-house mascot. 

It's all about the $$, doesn't make sense otherwise to remove such an intrinsic part of the Tokyo experience.

And to add, Chiharu has created other slightly different penguins which will still be out there after Suica's penguin is retired.

Based on my reading, it seems that what’s needed at the core may be both recalibrated fiscal policy and growth-oriented monetary policy.

Given the level of the national debt and the credit-heavy nature of the consumer economy, the Fed might want to consider pursuing policies that lower interest rates to curb any lingering concerns of a potential illiquidity or insolvency situation leading to currency and bond crises - however unlikely that may be - as well as to avoid triggering slower growth or a recession.

At the same time, the government should look into using targeted fiscal and regulatory solutions to raise taxes on upper-middle-class and wealthy households, perhaps by reducing various tax deductions. The government could also consider raising the federal estate tax rate while simultaneously lowering the exemption from the current $15 million.

While the debt limit is largely a symbolic and political measure that could eventually be removed, I wonder about the timing of it and how abolishing it now might be perceived by the market in terms of its perceived potential influence on inflation.

That’s my two cents.

This fund came from years of work by Panguna’s own communities, and that deserves credit. It might also be worth asking why a company comes back to the table when no court can force it. Perhaps the answer lies ahead, not behind. A company with future interests in a region may find a settled past useful when it seeks consent for new projects.
Panguna is not only copper. There is gold and silver in the ore, and these extra metals often decide whether a mine pays. The regional government has already brought in a new partner to reopen it.
We tend to read this as a story about one company. But the demand comes from us. Much of the world’s gold goes to jewelry, investment bars and central bank vaults, not clean energy. Less than half of the copper in old products is recycled. So the green transition still runs through places like Bougainville, where the cost has landed on the community in extreme environmental damage and a brutal civil war.
$250 million for 25,000 people and a buried river system is a start. Is it possible to call a transition just if it repeats this sequence somewhere else? Perhaps society as a whole needs to take more responsibility.

This includes a number of unstable political coalitions of all possible hues which really didn't care about the people (until recently replaced by a govt. after a gen-z rebellion). It also has few means of generating employment for its people and its politicians don't seem to care. Bangladesh next door - another poor country - has managed to increase its gdp per capita over the years with textile and other factories. And Nepal which played India against China to try to obtain benefits from both seems to have annoyed both of them.

comments.name: Erik Frederiksen
comments.body:
Nepal got hit very hard by the collapse of one of the many glaciers in the Himalayan mountains.

What the wealthy countries don't seem to understand is that no country will be immune to climate breakdown. This isn't some theoretical issue for the 22nd century or beyond, it's happening now.

Any child born now could potentially see all the remaining years of this century. That might not be very pleasant.

Climate change is becoming climate breakdown and the next stage is climate chaos, when seasons are scrambled, agriculture fails in many places, and eventually fails everywhere.

Nothing like this climatic transformation has happened for tens of millions of years. (1)

When the agricultural system collapses because of climate chaos, people will wish the politicians in every country had listened to scientists. Of course the politicians will blame the scientists for not warning them, lying as usual.

Then the real mass migrations will overwhelm everything.
1. https://www.livescience.com/oldest-climate-record-ever-cenozoic-era.html

comments.name: Erik Frederiksen
comments.body:
During this recent flood in Nepal the glacier involved lost only about 1 percent of its volume and there are around 50,000 such glaciers in the Himalayan mountains so we can begin to see the scale of the problem as our planet continues to rapidly heat. 

The Himalayas have been called the "Third Pole" because there is a tremendous amount of ice in the glaciers there. So the frequency and severity of these events are projected to increase significantly over the coming decades. 

Mountain glaciers are also important for water supply and this is already becoming a problem in many places.

comments.name: RDJ
comments.body:
Gene expression is one thing. The interaction of the gene products is quite another.

Many genes produce mRNA messages that are translated into proteins. Some of these proteins have enzymatic activity that underlies metabolism, and structural properties that underlies . . . Well, structure. Some of them have inhibitory or promoting effects on the activity of other proteins, or on the expression of other genes.

Other genes produce non-protein-coding RNAs that may have enzymatic activity themselves, or have excitatory or inhibitory effects on gene expression or protein translation.

And there are many small molecules that participate in these interactions. ATP, cAMP, cGMP, calcium and magnesium, and others. Their levels are regulated by protein activity.

All of these factors form an extremely complex network of positive and negative interactions. And all this goes on in the context of a membrane-enclosed space, within which there are other structures that serve specific purposes (mitochondria, Golgi apparatus, etc.)

Genes are the seeds; the cell is an entire rain forest.

A working model of the cell must include the details of this network. I cannot tell from this article whether these virtual cells do or not.
